title: Binomial-tail lower bound for hitting probability
statement: Let $V$ be a finite set, let $G$ be a directed graph on $V$, and define the out-neighbors of a vertex by its directed edges. For a symmetric relation $r$ on $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $B_D(m,j)$ be given by $B_D(m,0)=0$, $B_D(0,j+1)=1$, and $B_D(m+1,j+1)=B_D(m,j)/D+(1-1/D)B_D(m,j+1)$; let the padded graph use $D$ edge slots per vertex, sending slots beyond the first $n$ to the vertex itself. For every $m,j$ and starting vertex $s$, the hitting probability of a target $t$ in $G$ after $j$ independent uniform out-neighbor steps, minus $B_D(m,j)$, is at most the hitting probability of $t$ after $m$ such steps in the padded graph, provided $n\le D$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is finite and has decidable equality
$G$ is a directed graph on $V$ with decidable adjacency
$r$ is a decidable symmetric relation on $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$
$D$ is a natural number with $n\le D$
The inequality holds for every pair of natural numbers $m,j$ and every starting vertex $s$
